11. (Currently amended) A __computer-implemented__ method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; and generating, __with a computer processor,__ a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm, wherein the pseudo partial ordering of molecules is provided to the selected machine learning algorithm, and wherein __a computer processor executes__ the selected machine learning algorithm, using the pseudo partial ordering, __to__ train[[s]] a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model, __wherein the pseudo partial ordering comprises a set of ordered tuples of molecules selected from a plurality of molecules based on property measurements that each assign a value for the property of interest relative to a single molecule.__

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter.

13. (Previously presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a classification learning algorithm.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a __kernel-based__ learning algorithm __selected from a support vector machines algorithm or a modification thereof modified to process the pseudo partial ordering.__

15. (Previously presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof modified to process the pseudo partial ordering of ranked pairs.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, an area above, or below, a receiver operator characteristic curve, __and wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is executed by a computer processor.__

17. (Previously presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, a function of the rank ordering of molecules in the pseudo partial ordering.

18. (Previously presented) The method of claim 11, further comprising, determining an accuracy of the prediction for the additional molecule by carrying out laboratory experimentation using physically existing samples of the additional molecule, or by performing a research study using physical samples of the additional molecule.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules comprises: generating a vector representation of the molecules, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure of the molecules included __in__ the pseudo-partial ordering; or comprises generating an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein a threshold value or cutoff molecule is selected for the molecular properties model and used to create a classification model, __wherein the threshold value or cutoff molecule defines the ordered relative relationship of the first and second molecule with respect to the property of interest.__

21. (Previously presented) The method of claim 11, wherein the at least one additional molecule comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are alternative representations of the same physical molecule and the property of interest is a property of the alternative representations, __wherein said training set comprises said pseudo-partial ordering.__

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are encoded to represent different atoms, bonds or substituent groups of the same molecule and the property of interest is a property of the atoms, bonds or substituent groups, __wherein said training set comprises said pseudo-partial ordering.__

35. (Currently amended) A __non-transitory computer-storage medium__ containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; and generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm, wherein the pseudo partial ordering of molecules is provided to the selected machine learning algorithm, and wherein executing the selected machine learning algorithm, using the pseudo partial ordering, trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model, __wherein the pseudo partial ordering comprises a set of ordered tuples of molecules selected from a plurality of molecules based on property measurements that each assign a value for the property of interest relative to a single molecule.__
